name: Iodine Global Network: salt iodization support (charityevals, 2025)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: shares of the result at the defaults by branch, each split by births: policy reviews and tools 21% (India 83% of its births, then Tanzania, Cameroon, Germany, South Sudan, Sri Lanka and smaller countries), Lebanon 31%, Vietnam 26%, producer quality assurance 15% (Bolivia, Madagascar, Mozambique, northern Argentina and Peru by the births reached), regional advocacy 6% (South Asia's four uncounted countries, five large European countries and North America by births; a judgment), Davao City under 1%.
summary: The Iodine Global Network (IGN) helps governments and salt producers keep salt iodized: in 2025, spending $1.32 million, it brought Lebanon's main producers back to national standards, improved small producers' salt in Bolivia, northern Argentina and Madagascar, gave evidence behind Vietnam's Ministry of Health recommending that iodized salt stay compulsory in processed foods (the final decree is still being drafted), helped Davao City restart salt enforcement, reviewed laws or applied its monitoring tools in 19 countries, and pressed for iodine policy in Europe, South Asia and North America. Each piece of work is valued by the births it moves from iodine deficiency to protection (the reviews and advocacy in new rules the size of Moldova's requirement of iodized salt in bread, one every two and every four years): 7.5 IQ points lost to deficiency, halved for the milder deficiency at stake, worth 0.67% higher earnings per point over 40 working years, plus goitre averted less hyperthyroidism caused, counted for the years a won change counts (producer support for two or three) and credited by IGN's share of the resources behind it. The result, about 2.4 years of healthy life per 1,000 dollars, is very uncertain and rests mostly on judgment (how many new rules the reviews and advocacy lead to, how much mild deficiency harms cognition, whether Vietnam's final decree keeps the requirement); every branch is discounted for missing data, since no change in iodine status is measured, and the next dollar counts at 56% of the past average.

IQ points lost by a child born and raised iodine deficient (moderate to severe deficiency)
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: iodine): 7.5 points, the corrected best estimate of Bougma et al.'s meta-analysis of trials and cohorts in children up to five, mostly in moderate to severe deficiency.

rows.label: Loss in the deficiency IGN's countries risk, relative to the meta-analysis's
rows.explainer: Our judgment, for children who would be deficient (the branches count only those). The deficiency IGN's work prevents is mostly mild to moderate (pregnant women below the adequate range in Vietnam, Madagascar and Lebanon; small producers' under-iodized salt in Bolivia and Argentina), milder than the meta-analysis's mostly moderate-to-severe settings. Anchors within deficient children: Feyrer, Politi and Weil (2017) find US iodization raised IQ by about a standard deviation (15 points) in the most deficient quarter, where deficiency was severe, the high end's direction; Gowachirapant et al. (2017) found daily iodine for mildly deficient pregnant women in India and Thailand made no difference to children's IQ at five to six (verbal IQ −0.7 points, 95% CI −2.9 to 1.5), the low end's. Half the meta-analysis's loss, 3.75 points (a quarter to nine tenths).

rows.label: Increase in adult earnings per IQ point
rows.explainer: The shared figure from GiveWell's iron sheets (0.67% per point), the one every cognition-to-income model on the site reads.

rows.label: Gain in ln(earnings) per year of working life, per child protected
rows.explainer: IQ points kept times the earnings gain per point, as a log gain in consumption, the unit the site values income in.

rows.label: Years from protection in pregnancy and infancy to the start of earnings
rows.explainer: The shared figure (facts: iodine): about 15 years, when a child protected in the womb and in infancy starts working.

rows.label: Years the earnings gain lasts
rows.explainer: GiveWell's house figure for long-term income gains from childhood health (40 years), shared by every such model on the site.

rows.label: Multiplier for earnings shared within the household
rows.explainer: GiveWell's house figure (2): an earner's extra income is shared with the household, so it raises others' consumption too. Read by every later-life income chain on the site.

rows.label: Value of the earnings gain per child protected (units of value)
rows.explainer: The yearly log gain over 40 working years, discounted at your rate from when the child starts work, times household sharing and the shared value of a log unit of consumption.

rows.label: Illness averted per child protected (goitre, hypothyroidism), in healthy years
rows.explainer: Our judgment, counted as healthy years and bridged below, with no wait (the illness comes in childhood, not when earnings start). GBD counts iodine deficiency's burden almost wholly as disability, visible goitre with or without hypothyroidism. In mild to moderate deficiency WHO's grading puts goitre in 5% to 30% of schoolchildren; a deficient child's chance of visible goitre of about 10%, lasting about ten years, at a disability weight of about 0.02 gives 0.02 healthy years (0.005 to 0.06). Deaths and stillbirths from severe deficiency are not counted: rare at the deficiency at stake.

rows.label: Iodine-induced hyperthyroidism in older adults, per child protected (a harm), in healthy years
rows.explainer: Our judgment, a side effect, counted now (no wait). Raising iodine intake in a deficient population briefly raises hyperthyroidism among older adults with nodular goitre: Feyrer, Politi and Weil (2017) find thyroid deaths rose after US iodization, mostly among older people in deficient areas. Per child protected there are about 60 people in the population whose intake rises (a birth rate near 16 per 1,000); a few extra cases per 10,000 of them for a year or two at a moderate disability weight gives about −0.002 healthy years where iodization is introduced. Most of IGN's work restores or keeps intake that populations had until recently, where the excess is smaller: −0.001 (−0.005 to 0).

rows.label: Healthy years per child protected (illness averted less hyperthyroidism)
rows.explainer: Illness averted plus the hyperthyroidism harm (a side effect, which your side-effect slider weights), in healthy years; they reach units of value only through the bridge below.

rows.label: Years a won change counts before it would have come anyway
rows.explainer: The site's one answer (Your values → How impact is counted; docs/normalization.md 2.9). Never the charity's or an evaluator's own years. Branches whose gain may not last that long (producer support) cap it at their own persistence.

rows.label: Probability the change happens because of this work
rows.explainer: Each branch carries its own chances in its counterfactual rows (Vietnam's decree as single events), so this canonical row is 1.

rows.label: Producer quality assurance: share of these births whose salt moves from under- to adequately iodized
rows.explainer: Our judgment. These producers already iodize; the work (plant visits, training, better premixing and rotary mixers, less iodine lost in production, joint buying of potassium iodate) raised salt quality over time, and Madagascar's supported producers moved gradually toward standard. A tenth of the households they supply (3% to 30%) move from under-iodized to adequate salt.

rows.label: Producer quality assurance: share of those births that would be deficient with under-iodized salt
rows.explainer: Our judgment. Under-iodized salt still carries some iodine, and other foods some more; north-west Argentina and Bolivia's highlands have a history of severe deficiency, Madagascar's pregnant women remain deficient in some regions (2024 survey). Two fifths (a fifth to seven tenths).

rows.label: Producer quality assurance: years the producers' gain lasts once the support stops
rows.explainer: Our judgment. This is ongoing technical help to producers alongside government monitoring, and the gain came over time with continued visits; mixers and routines are capital and habit that last, but iodate prices and staff turnover wear them down. Two years (one to five), capped at the years a won change counts.

rows.label: Births a Moldova-sized rule protects, as a share of its country's births
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the size of the unit the two advocacy branches count in: a rule like Moldova's requirement of iodized salt in bread (in force since 2011 and re-issued in December 2025 after IGN's processed-food assessment), with bread an estimated 40% to 70% of iodine intake and compliance high (p. 37). Such a rule moves about half of a country's births (three to seven tenths) from deficient to adequate intake. The unit is a hypothetical new rule of that size; Moldova's own re-issue isn't counted as one.

rows.label: Births a year one Moldova-sized rule protects
rows.explainer: Moldova's births a year times the share a rule like its bread rule protects: about 12,700 births, the unit the two advocacy branches count their wins in.

rows.label: Policy reviews and tools: new Moldova-sized rules a year they lead to
rows.explainer: Our judgment, in new rules the size of Moldova's bread rule (each protecting about 12,700 births a year): what a year's law and standard reviews (India, Germany, the Maldives, South Sudan), program assessments, sentinel surveillance and processed-food assessments in the 19 toolkit countries lead to. The report shows findings and plans (Bhutan's processed-food gap, Sri Lanka's follow-up surveillance, the Maldives' outdated data, South Sudan's draft strategy) but no new rule from the tools in 2019-2025 (Moldova's bread rule dates from 2011): one such rule every two years, from one a decade to two a year (a review in India that changes its standards would count as many).

Trust in the iodine-to-earnings chain (all branches)
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the product of two parts: the IQ gap is partly from cohort studies, where deficient families differ in other ways (0.85), and whether early IQ gains persist into adult earnings as the per-point wage figure assumes (0.8). 0.7 (0.45 to 0.9); anchored on GiveWell's own salt iodization model, whose internal and external validity (0.8 × 0.7) and share of the benefit lasting (0.8) together give 0.45, here with the setting's milder deficiency already in the severity row.

rows.label: Vietnam: chance the final decree keeps the processed-food requirement
rows.explainer: Our judgment, a single event. The report says the Ministry of Health recommended maintaining mandatory fortification under Decree 09/2016, but the amending decree is still being drafted (consultation on 31 March 2026), a 2018 government resolution had directed that the requirement be abolished, and seafood and export industries keep lobbying for exemptions. 60% (30% to 85%) that the final text keeps it substantially intact.
